purpose: Assemble one project SSOT document from typed evidence and interview answers. Do not crawl a live repository.

questions.prompt: What is the stable project id? (e.g. wellmanifest.ssot or subactor.widget)
What is the human-facing project name?
What SemVer should the description document declare?
placement.home: which org HOMEs this repository? Use an id from registry/homes.json (add yours there rather than editing schemas). "w ramach wellmanifest" means ADOPT, not HOME.
placement.shape: domain_pack | runtime_service | both. runtime_service must not HOME wellmanifest.
placement.runtimeOwner: who runs the CLI/daemon? Same enum as home. Empty inherits home. wellmanifest does not host product daemons.
placement.adopt: which wellmanifest packs to follow? (comma-separated wellmanifest/<pack> ids). ADOPT is not HOME.
One sentence: what is this project for? This is the field humans get wrong when README and schema disagree.
Who owns semantics? (comma-separated ids, e.g. github:wellmanifest/ssot)
If evidence sources disagree on purpose, which source id wins? (dsl-manifest, intent, interview, or empty if purpose above is the resolution)
How does README relate to this document?
If README or marketing copy may differ from schema purpose, what is the KNOWN_DIVERGENT reason? (empty if identical)
Is a code2llm TOON, map.toon.yaml, or other analyzer artifact listed in the evidence index?
If yes, which analyzer? (code2llm-toon, map-toon-yaml, redup, other, none)
Should analyzer output stay evidence-only until a human confirms it? (almost always yes)
Has a human confirmed analyzer hits are real description debt, not noise?

capability.verbs: what does this project DO? 1-8 from: analyze, audit, discover, index, query, generate, transform, convert, document, package, validate, test, lint, repair, refactor, plan, orchestrate, execute, schedule, deploy, serve, monitor, publish, sync.
capability.keywords: up to 12 discriminating terms. Not the category - the words that tell this project apart from its siblings.
capability.useWhen: 1-6 concrete situations where this is the right project to reach for.
capability.doNotUseWhen: 1-6 situations where reaching for this is a mistake, and what to reach for instead. Name the misreading its own name invites.
capability.install.status: how does a consumer obtain a working invocation? (pypi | npm | binary | src-only | container | none). src-only means PYTHONPATH or equivalent is required.
capability.install.package: the published package name, if status is pypi/npm/container.
capability.entrypoints: the primary way to run it, as 'kind:name:invoke' (e.g. cli:diagit:diagit audit --root ~/github).
capability.maturity.level: experimental | beta | stable | maintenance | deprecated.
capability.stacks: stack profile ids this project belongs to (feeds intent.json stacks).
capability.siblings: related projects as 'id:relation[:target]' (relations: invokes, extends, overlaps, superseded-by, supersedes, exports-to, facade-of, depends-on, alternative-to).
